transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-27
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Miguel (Redwood SE), Jordan (AetherGrid CTO), Mei (AetherGrid Lead Infra), Carlos (AetherGrid Product), Emma (AetherGrid Security)

Summary:
Quick handoff to align on marketplace packaging + reference architecture for AetherGrid's connector that will enable Redwood Private/Dedicated via their marketplace listing. Focus: networking/VPC, KMS integration, packaging (helm + OCI image), UAT plan, and initial perf benchmarks. Action items and next steps agreed at end.

Topics covered:
- Marketplace listing artifact checklist and tile content
- Networking (VPC peering, NAT, egress, firewall rules)
- KMS/HSM and key rotation for Redwood Private connector
- Packaging: helm chart, container image layout, ingress patterns
- Benchmarks: throughput/latency expectations and test harness
- Security & compliance preflight (SOC2, audit logs, SSO/SAML)
- UAT + roll-out plan and timeline

Transcript body (imperfect automatic transcription, timestamps approximate):
[00:00:04] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we wanted to do a concise run through of the onramp so that AetherGrid can get the marketplace tile published and also have our refarch guide lined up. Jordan, Mei, you good to kick off?
[00:00:18] Jordan: Yeah thanks, Samir. Quick context: AetherGrid builds data fabric for edge infra, looking to list a connector in the Redwood marketplace so customers can easily deploy Redwood Private into their VPCs. We have an initial helm chart and a container image, but need to align on KMS, routing, and the OOM, uh, the operational expectations.
[00:00:35] Priya: Cool. From Redwood side we'll want to validate three things in the UAT: networking reachability (peering and egress), KMS integration (we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer-managed HSM workflows), and smoke benchmarks for latency under realistic prefix-cache scenarios.
[00:00:50] Mei: Quick question — for KMS we assume we need to create grants so Redwood can encrypt model keys, or do you expect the customer to pass a key?
[00:00:59] Miguel: In the Private deployment pattern we usually have the customer create keys and give Redwood a decrypt/grant via cross-account role, or if they deploy fully on-prem then they point to their HSM. We'll share the exact IAM policy and sample grant.
[00:01:15] Carlos: Also, on the marketplace tile we need clarity on the pricing callouts. Is there a recommended language — like dedicated vs hosted?
[00:01:22] Samir: For the tile we put 'Redwood Private connector' and then call out 'bring-your-own infra; pricing through AetherGrid' or 'integration fee' — the specifics you decide, but we'll provide a recommended blurb. We'll also put sample architecture diagrams in the refarch doc.
[00:01:38] Jordan: Sounds good. Can you confirm whether network egress from customer to Redwood control plane is required? Our security team is sensitive to any outbound paths.
[00:01:47] Priya: For marketplace listing + onboarding we try to minimize control-plane egress; there is an option for the 'air-gapped' flow where control plane calls are minimal — most teams use a lightweight control channel for rollout and observability, but data plane (model inference) stays inside the customer's VPC for Private. We'll document both flows.
[00:02:05] Emma: If there's control-plane telemetry, we need to know what flows out: metrics only, no PII, and if possible hashed IDs. Also retention windows.
[00:02:14] Miguel: Agreed. We typically send token-level cost metrics and anonymized latency histograms; no payload. Retention defaults to 90 days but that can be negotiated for enterprise.
[00:02:27] Mei: Ok, that helps. For the helm chart, there is a CRD we added for KV cache configuration — will Redwood's runtime need any special annotations to prefer our cache?
[00:02:36] Priya: We expect an annotation to point to the local KV endpoint; that's fine. We'll need a migration test where we run prefix-cache warmup and observe hit-rate. Priya: I'll prepare a small test plan.
[00:02:51] Jordan: On benchmarking — what's the realistic throughput we should aim for during UAT? We were aiming for 200 concurrent tokens-per-second for a 4 GPU cluster.
[00:03:00] Priya: For reference, our dedicated profiles: on A100/80GB-ish we see X tokens/sec depending on batch; but for your initial UAT I'd recommend a steady-state test at 150-250 tokens/sec with mixed sequence lengths and a short tail latency SLO of 300ms P95 for small LLMs. We'll give you a harness (JMeter + custom client) — link: https://redwood.example/harness (note: placeholder).
[00:03:22] Jordan: Perfect.
[00:03:26] Carlos: On the listing UX — we need a short product blurb and three use cases. Any constraints on wording, like mention of 'beta' or 'certified'?
[00:03:34] Samir: We can mark it 'Redwood-verified' after we finish the compatibility checklist and smoke tests. Initially it can be 'preview'. We'll give a template for the blurb.
[00:03:44] Emma: Security artifacts: we have SOC2 Type II but need to map gaps to Redwood requirements — can you share a list of required docs?
[00:03:52] Miguel: We'll share the security onboarding pack: SOC2 summary, pen-test results, KMS integration docs, SSO/SAML flows, and audit log schema. We'll also note acceptable evidence for each.
[00:04:07] Mei: One nit: our cluster is multi-tenant and uses egress NAT. For the VPC peering path, do you require specific ports to be open or only TLS outbound?
[00:04:16] Priya: TLS outbound on 443 is enough for the minimal control channel. For data plane models we recommend direct VPC routing (peered or private link); we'll add a sample SG (security group) snippet to the refarch.
[00:04:29] Jordan: Great. Let's talk packaging — we currently publish an OCI image at ghcr.io/aethergrid/rg-connector:latest and a helm chart. We plan to add an operator later. Is helm-only fine for initial listing?
[00:04:41] Samir: Helm is fine for the first pass. For marketplace we usually want a helm chart + a small integration test that runs as a post-install job. Also a README that includes the 'runbook' for upgrades and rollback.
[00:04:56] Miguel: We also require a small healthcheck endpoint /_redwood/health that the market-verified CI will scrape. It's just a 200 with a JSON payload.
[00:05:06] Mei: We can add that.
[00:05:10] Carlos: Any requirements around license headers or disclaimers?
[00:05:14] Samir: Not strict; just make sure the licensing is clear and the tile states support contact info. Marketplace will display contact to AetherGrid for initial leads.
[00:05:22] Jordan: About the refarch doc — can Redwood include a sample 'typical deployment' with quantization recommendations? We run customers on 4xH100 sometimes and prefer int8 quant on certain models.
[00:05:33] Priya: We'll put a quantization section with recommended model families and target hardware, and note tradeoffs — quality vs perf. Also include KV cache sizing guidance; many partners forget the cache sizing table.
[00:05:45] Emma: For audit logs, is there a standard schema we should export from our side?
[00:05:49] Miguel: Yes, we'll share the audit log schema: request_id, timestamp, model_id, route, anonymized_user_hash, tokens_in/out, and status codes. No prompt text.
[00:05:59] Mei: On SSO — marketplace onboarding will need SAML metadata exchange so Redwood console users can be mapped to partner orgs?
[00:06:06] Samir: Correct — if you want a joint tenant experience we'll exchange SAML metadata. For now, the listing can be self-serve and then enterprise customers can opt into SSO.
[00:06:16] Jordan: Ok, timeline question — if we finish the checklist by first week of September can we aim to be in marketplace preview by mid-September?
[00:06:23] Samir: Yes that's realistic: checklist by 2026-09-01, UAT week 2026-09-07, preview week of 2026-09-14. We'll treat any security gaps as blockers for 'verified' status, but preview is fine.
[00:06:38] Carlos: One more thing — will Redwood run a compatibility smoke test against our chart in a sandbox?
[00:06:43] Priya: Yes. We'll spin up a sandbox cluster, install your chart, run the health checks and the small throughput test. That will be the basis for a 'Redwood Verified' badge.
[00:06:53] Emma: On the topic of telemetry retention — if we want 30-day retention instead of 90 for certain customers, is that configurable per-account?
[00:06:59] Miguel: Yes, for enterprise customers retention is configurable; it's an SLA discussion.
[00:07:06] Jordan: Great. Anything else?
[00:07:09] Samir: Let's recap action items — I'll share the listing checklist and a sample helm chart repo link. Priya will run the perf harness in your dev cluster — Mei will hand over networking details and Emma will run through security docs. Carlos will draft product blurb. We'll aim for preview in mid-September.
[00:07:27] Mei: Quick clarifying question — for KMS cross-account, do you have a template CloudFormation or Terraform?
[00:07:33] Miguel: We'll share a Terraform snippet and the IAM policy.
[00:07:37] Jordan: Awesome, thanks everyone.
[00:07:40] Samir: Thanks, we'll follow up with the drive link and schedule the UAT slot.
